content:
mel: Starting canary for Borealis-20B (ptq-int4) on dedicated-pool-a. Initial runs ok but hit 2 OOMs ~2500 tokens in, memory fragmentation spike. dumping notes here :eyes:
ci-bot: canary-deploy: borealis-20b@ptq-int4 -> pool:dedicated-pool-a, commit:ff3a2e, started 4187654321
mel: attaching the small OOM snippet we saw:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] ERR OOM: alloc failed for new_kv_buffer size=48MB
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] INFO kv_cache stats: used=1.9GB, free_chunks=12, frag=0.42
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] WARN attempting kv_trim -> failed to reclaim contiguous block
```
tanvi: hmm frag=0.42 at ~2GB used. sounds like prefetch + large max_new_tokens combo. what was the request shape?
mel: mostly long-chat synth tests; default max_new_tokens=1024, typical prompt ~800 tokens, so some sessions end up 1800-2000 tokens.
raj: first quick mitigation: reduce default max_new_tokens for this model to 512 for canary and set a conservative batch cap. cheaper and less risky while we root cause. :+1:
sam: also try disabling KV prefetch on the canary and enable aggressive kv_trim after each response to defragment. in config: 
```
model_config:
  max_new_tokens: 512
  batching:
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    max_items: 6
  prefetch_kv: false
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.65
  kv_trim_mode: aggressive
```
julia: quick note about perf/quality — reducing max_new_tokens might truncate some long completions; add a prompt-based guard to request higher max only for verified long-session clients, not global default.
tanvi: agree. we can gate with routing rule: if client in beta-longchat allow max_new_tokens up to 2048 else default 512.
mel: applied the config as a canary patch: `rdeploy canary --model borealis-20b --config /tmp/borealis-20b-canary-slo.yaml`
ci-bot: canary-config-update: borealis-20b applied to dedicated-pool-a (change-id: cfg-7d2b)
raj: also bump kv compaction interval to be more frequent for this model (every 30s) to observe fragmentation curve.
sam: ran a quick local repro with synthetic multi-turn workload. fragmentation still increases but kv_trim=aggressive lowers peak by ~18% and eliminated the OOM in 30 runs. logs: `frag_peak_before=0.44 frag_peak_after=0.36`
julia: perf regression check: ran our eval suite on canary vs baseline — latency + p95 +12ms, quality delta metric (ROUGE-ish) within noise (~0.2%). I think acceptable for now.
mel: current plan: keep canary for 6 hours, monitor mem frag, OOMs, and user-visible quality. if stable, promote to dedicated default but keep routing/gates for long-chat.
tanvi: add alert if frag >0.5 or OOM count >1 in 1h window. I can add Prom rule.
mel: thanks, tanvi. I'll post a short follow-up if we need rollback. :thumbsup:
sam: two follow-ups for later: (1) run PTQ with alternative kernel ordering to reduce allocation churn, (2) try small reserved page for KV to reduce external fragmentation. i'll spin tickets.
mel: nice, thanks everyone. will keep thread updated.
raj: thanks, closing loop for now :rocket:
